questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far a vehicle needs to stop?

options.text: The condition and type of your tires.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for possible hazards. Do not stare only at the road directly ahead. Scan ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: Adults 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving while impaired is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a yellow circular light.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a yellow circular light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow has the same meaning as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and prepare for a red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off fog and shine back into your eyes.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slide to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT make night driving safer?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking at oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is difficult because you cannot see behind your vehicle easily. Before backing up, walk to the back to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for the walk signal.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicycles, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: How far away from a crosswalk must you park?
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 25 feet of a crosswalk or intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means you cannot do that action. This sign means U-turns are not permitted in this location.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process in one hour?
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies process about one alcoholic drink per hour. However, how impaired you feel depends on many factors, including how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, whether you have eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you slow down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Right when you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed the same until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the posted speed for the exit ramp.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed and curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle may be hard to control in a curve if you are going too fast.

questions.question: Which traffic light means you must stop, yield to cross traffic, then go when it is safe?
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to all cross traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, enter the first lane.

questions.question: When can you make a left turn at a red light?

options.text: When turning from a two-way street to a two-way street.
When turning from a one-way street to another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning from a one-way street to another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After you stop completely, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Do not enter the intersection until you can pass all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can pass all the way through.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection if you cannot drive completely through it. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will also have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: How should you always treat railroad crossings?

options.text: Safe to cross, since trains rarely come.
Safe places to park your car.
A place where you must always stop.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and flagger directions. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You park facing uphill on a street with a curb. After setting the parking brake, what should you do with your front wheels?

options.text: Turn them away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: You are driving on an interstate. Traffic is merging from an on-ramp on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.

questions.explanation: Watch for on-ramps ahead on interstate highways. When it is safe, move to the left lane to let vehicles enter from the on-ramp on your right.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
